notes.text: Jonathan Marchessault is day to day (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 6 games. He is a top-six forward.

Nicolas Hague has not dressed for the last 7 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Daemon Hunt has taken his spot beside Jayden Struble. That pair has had 41% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 83:43 together, up from 29% with Hague.
Shane Wright joined from SEA on Nov 2 and has played beside Filip Forsberg and Nils Höglander.
Adam Edström has started killing penalties: on the ice for 32% of the team’s shorthanded time in 20 games, up from 1% with his old team last season.
Joel Eriksson Ek is day to day (upper-body injury), reported after he played in their last game. He is a top-six forward.

stakes: The Predators go in second in the Central with 27 points, 5 points behind the Wild, first.

MIN.head: Advantage, the Wild
MIN.body: Minnesota has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Predators can make it interesting if their penalty kill holds up.

NSH.head: The Predators have a hill to climb
NSH.body: Minnesota has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Predators’ best way through is a penalty kill that holds up.

story.head: Stamkos’s favorite opponent
paras: The Predators are on a tear, seven straight wins. Minnesota has won two in a row. The Wild won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-1 in Nashville on Oct 1. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Preds second (tied for eighth in the NHL) and the Wild first (tied for first).

The Predators’ record (.675) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.531), largely thanks to their goaltending. So is the Wild’s (.762 on chances worth .652), largely thanks to their goaltending.
In their seven-game winning streak, the Predators have outscored teams 23-12, including 17-10 at 5-on-5.

The Wild (32nd) and the Predators (31st) both get pinned in their own end on long shifts. The Predators keep things calm after the whistle (2nd lowest). Nashville has allowed 2.60 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. The Wild let the point shots come and guard the net (2nd) and leave the shooting to their forwards (3rd lowest). Minnesota has allowed 2.19 goals a game, the fewest in the league. The Wild are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Predators. Beyond that, both teams like to play fast, especially the Predators (3rd), so expect an open game.

Roman Josi (2 G / 21 A / 23 P in 20 GP) leads the Predators in scoring. Steven Stamkos (11 G / 10 A / 21 P in 20 GP) has a team-high eleven goals, with a point in nine straight games against Minnesota. Kirill Kaprizov (17 G / 18 A / 35 P in 21 GP) leads the Wild in scoring and is third in the NHL, with ten points in his last five games. Quinn Hughes (6 G / 22 A / 28 P in 21 GP) is next in line, with seven points in his last five games.

Juuse Saros (7-3-4 / .922 SV% in 14 GS) has been a rock in net for Nashville and will likely start. Jesper Wallstedt (13-2-3 / .925 SV% in 18 GS) has been a rock in net for Minnesota and will likely start.
The Wild usually control more of the chances than the Predators do.
